issues.legal_issue: A party that conceded an instrument was a kanom under an earlier statute could not dispute that classification under a later statute whose definition was materially the same.
material_facts: In the High Court, the appellants expressly conceded that the 1929 instrument was a kanom within the meaning of the then-applicable agrarian statute.
The later statute defined kanom in materially the same terms as the earlier statute.
issues.conclusion: The instrument had to be treated as a kanom under the later statute.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the appellants’ concession and the substantial identity between the definitions of kanom in Section 2(18) of the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960 and Section 2(22) of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

predicates.appeal_case: The dispute is before a court in an appeal.
predicates.party_conceded_classification_below: A party expressly accepted the instrument’s legal classification in a lower-court proceeding.
predicates.governing_definitions_materially_same: The applicable later definition is materially the same as the definition under which the party made its concession.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an instrument that a party classified in a lower-court proceeding under a materially equivalent definition, the instrument is treated as having that classification.

issues.legal_issue: A registered instrument styled as a release may transfer property rights when its terms and circumstances establish an intention to transfer those rights for valuable consideration.
material_facts: The instrument was registered and was styled a release deed concerning kanom rights.
The transferee paid consideration to the transferor.
The operative wording stated that the transferor’s rights, liabilities, and claims under the earlier instruments were surrendered to the transferee.
The instrument disclosed an intention to transfer the transferor’s kanom rights, and its operative words were capable of passing title.
issues.conclusion: The release deed operated as an assignment of the kanom rights.
issues.legal_principle: A deed’s substance and operative terms, rather than its title alone or the stamp used, determine whether it transfers rights. The Court distinguished Mt. Oodey Koowur v. Mt. Ladoo, 13 Moo Ind App 585 (PC), where a bare admission without consideration did not convey a subsequently acquired title, and the release or relinquishment cases Jadu Nath Poddar v. Rup Lal Poddar, ILR 33 Cal 967, Dharam Chand v. Mauji Sahu, 16 Cal LJ 436, Narak Lall v. Magoo Lall, and Mathuramohan Saha v. Ram Kumar Saha. Those authorities did not establish that a document styled a release can never convey property. The Court relied on Hemendra Nath Mukerji v. Kumar Nath Roy, 12 Cal WN 478, in which a registered deed styled a disclaimer was construed as a transfer, and held that a release deed for valuable consideration may operate as a conveyance if it clearly manifests an intention to transfer.

rule.if: property_rights_dispute and registered_instrument and valuable_consideration_paid and instrument_discloses_transfer_intent and operative_words_capable_of_passing_title

predicates.property_rights_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether an instrument transferred rights in property.
predicates.valuable_consideration_paid: The transferee paid valuable consideration for the transfer.
predicates.instrument_discloses_transfer_intent: The instrument’s terms and circumstances show that the parties intended to transfer the transferor’s rights to the transferee.
predicates.operative_words_capable_of_passing_title: The operative wording is capable of transferring the rights in question.

issues.definition: In a property-rights dispute, a registered instrument supported by valuable consideration operates as a conveyance when its terms show an intention to transfer and its operative words can pass title.

issues.legal_issue: An assignee of kanom rights is a tenant entitled to protection from eviction where the governing tenancy statute gives tenants fixity of tenure.
material_facts: The instrument creating the kanom rights was treated as a kanom under the governing statute.
A registered deed for consideration transferred the kanom rights to the contesting defendants.
The defendants thereby became kanomdars of the properties.
The governing statute included a kanomdar within the meaning of tenant and granted every tenant fixity of tenure, subject to its specified exceptions.
issues.conclusion: The contesting defendants were kanomdars and tenants protected from eviction under the governing statute, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(22) and 2(57) of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 define kanom and include a kanomdar within the definition of tenant. Section 13 gives every tenant fixity of tenure and prohibits resumption except as provided in Sections 14 to 22. Because the deed transferred the kanom rights, the assignees held those rights as kanomdars and were protected from eviction.

rule.if: tenancy_protection_dispute and kanom_rights_created and kanom_rights_validly_assigned and assignee_holds_kanom_rights

predicates.tenancy_protection_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a person holding land through kanom rights is protected from eviction.
predicates.kanom_rights_created: An instrument created rights that qualify as kanom rights under the applicable law.
predicates.kanom_rights_validly_assigned: The kanom rights were transferred to the person claiming protection by a valid assignment.
predicates.assignee_holds_kanom_rights: The person claiming protection holds the assigned kanom rights in the property.

issues.definition: In a dispute over tenancy protection, a person who validly receives and holds created kanom rights is treated as a tenant protected from eviction.
